paragraphs: MusclePose estimates three-dimensional human pose and movement dynamics from video recorded by a single camera. Its aim extends beyond locating joints: it also infers physically plausible forces and muscle signals. This is difficult because visible motion does not uniquely determine the forces producing it, especially without training data annotated with those forces.

The method combines two ways of estimating joint torques, the turning forces acting at joints. One uses Lagrange’s equations, while the other models muscle dynamics through muscle torque generators. This multiple-hypothesis design aims to make inferred kinetics more biologically faithful. MusclePose also predicts detailed body measurements informed by biomechanics studies, rather than constructing the body solely from simple geometric shapes.

The reported results show positional accuracy competitive with existing pose estimators, together with plausible kinetics and muscle signals consistent with biomechanics findings. The model learns end to end and does not require an external physics engine. Its contribution is therefore a way to connect visual pose estimation with richer biomechanical inference while retaining competitive joint-position estimates.
neurips-2025-3d-human-pose-estimation-wi.tldr: MusclePose combines motion equations and muscle modeling to estimate competitive 3D poses and plausible human kinetics from monocular video.

paragraphs: A randomized trial can estimate treatment effects for its participants while leaving open how those effects apply to a different population. This paper studies transporting causal measures when populations differ in their observed characteristics, a setting called covariate shift. It broadens the focus beyond risk differences to measures that express treatment effects in other clinically useful ways.

The proposed framework covers a broad class of population effects based on first moments, or averages. These include absolute and relative measures such as risk differences, risk ratios, and odds ratios. The authors establish identification results under two conditional exchangeability assumptions and derive both classical and semiparametric estimators. Those assumptions underpin when the desired target-population quantities can be recovered.

Theoretical analysis, simulations, and real-world applications examine the resulting estimators. A central finding is that estimator behavior depends on the effect measure: one-step and estimating-equation approaches produce similar estimators for risk differences but distinct ones for odds ratios. This makes the choice of causal measure consequential for statistical methodology as well as interpretation.
neurips-2025-a-unified-framework-for-the.tldr: The paper develops a common framework for transporting multiple population-level causal measures under covariate shift and conditional exchangeability assumptions.

paragraphs: Understanding individual images does not by itself establish that a multimodal model can reason consistently about an object seen from different viewpoints. Actial addresses this spatial reasoning problem through Viewpoint Learning, a task intended both to evaluate and improve these abilities. Cross-view consistency is central because three-dimensional reasoning requires reconciling changing appearances.

The authors introduce Viewpoint-100K, containing 100,000 object-centered image pairs with varied viewpoints and associated questions and answers. Training proceeds in two stages. Supervised fine-tuning first develops foundational spatial knowledge using this dataset. Reinforcement learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization then uses a broader collection of questions to improve generalization. A hybrid cold-start initialization is designed to support both viewpoint representations and coherent reasoning.

Experiments report improvements on reasoning tasks within and outside the training domain, with supervised fine-tuning already improving multiple tasks. These results support explicitly developing foundational spatial skills rather than assuming they follow automatically from strong two-dimensional understanding. The work points toward applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and scene understanding without claiming to have validated every such application.
neurips-2025-actial-activate-spatial-rea.tldr: Actial develops spatial reasoning through viewpoint-focused supervised training followed by reinforcement learning, improving both in-domain and out-of-domain tasks.

paragraphs: Exploration in an open world requires an agent to change its behavior as a task progresses. A strategy useful while searching may become inefficient once the goal is nearby. Cognitive Predictive Processing addresses the fixed exploration mechanisms and static transition thresholds that the authors identify as limitations of recent approaches.

The framework combines three systems inspired by human decision-making. A cognitive controller separates activity into exploration, approach, and completion phases and adjusts its parameters accordingly. A memory system balances immediate context with selectively retained long-term information. An uncertainty-sensitive prediction regulator continually revises expectations about the environment and uses them to adjust exploration. Together, these components connect task progress, remembered information, and uncertainty to action selection.

Experiments in MineDojo report an average 4.6% improvement in resource-collection success rates and an average 7.1% reduction in completion steps over recent techniques. These findings support the usefulness of adaptive exploration and selective memory in the evaluated tasks. The human-inspired structure functions as a practical design for sustained exploration and strategic adjustment.
neurips-2025-cognitive-predictive-proces.tldr: CPP coordinates task phases, selective memory, and uncertainty-aware predictions to improve exploration efficiency and success in MineDojo.

paragraphs: A coreset is a compact representation of a dataset intended to preserve its clustering costs. This paper studies constructing such representations when observations have been corrupted by random noise from a known distribution. The central difficulty is evaluating preservation quality when the clean dataset, whose clustering cost matters, is unavailable.

The authors address this through surrogate error measures that can be evaluated and mathematically connected to the true cost. They analyze a previous measure and introduce one that tracks the underlying clustering cost more closely. Although the new measure itself does not depend on the noise distribution, its approximation guarantees reflect the noise level. A construction algorithm uses this measure to select a coreset.

Under mild assumptions on the data and noise, bounding the new error measure yields smaller coresets and tighter true-cost guarantees than classical measures. The possible size improvement reaches a polynomial factor in the number of clusters. Experiments on real-world datasets support these theoretical findings, connecting the revised quality criterion to practical gains in compact clustering representations.
neurips-2025-coresets-for-clustering-und.tldr: A new surrogate error measure enables smaller clustering coresets with tighter guarantees under stated assumptions about stochastic noise and data.

paragraphs: Distributed training requires machines to exchange gradients so that their model updates remain coordinated. Compressing those gradients reduces communication volume, but very low precision can harm final accuracy. DUO addresses this tradeoff by changing when additional high-precision communication occurs, aiming to recover accuracy without adding execution overhead.

The framework inserts a high-precision gradient synchronization into a phase previously devoted only to computation. Its scheduling allows that communication to be fully overlapped with computation. The design therefore retains a more accurate synchronization signal while avoiding an exposed communication delay. The authors also provide a theoretical convergence proof and evaluate the approach through GPT pre-training experiments.

With four-bit gradient compression, the experiments report accuracy comparable to uncompressed training. They also find minimal degradation with one-bit gradients and when the low-precision communication step is omitted entirely. That zero-bit case still includes DUO’s high-precision synchronization; it does not mean training without communication. The results show how scheduling and precision can work together to reduce the accuracy penalty of compression.
neurips-2025-duo-no-compromise-to-accura.tldr: DUO overlaps high-precision gradient synchronization with computation to recover accuracy lost through aggressive gradient compression.

paragraphs: Long-term forecasting could benefit from more historical observations, but longer inputs also bring redundant information and noise. Transformers may spread attention too broadly or fit irrelevant fluctuations. This paper introduces Maximum Effective Window, a metric intended to measure how much historical context a forecasting model can actually use effectively.

The authors propose two modules to improve that capability. The Information Bottleneck Filter selects essential subsequences, reducing the amount of redundant or noisy information passed onward. Hybrid-Transformer-Mamba combines Mamba’s selective forgetting over long sequences with Transformer modeling over shorter sequences. These components address both the quality of the supplied history and the way the model processes it.

The modules are designed to work across models and are integrated into several Transformer-based forecasters. Experiments report increases in Maximum Effective Window alongside improved overall forecasting performance. The findings connect gains to making longer histories usable: expanding an input window alone may be less helpful than filtering it and providing mechanisms that selectively retain information.
neurips-2025-enhancing-the-maximum-effec.tldr: The paper measures usable forecasting history and expands it through information filtering and a hybrid Transformer–Mamba module.

paragraphs: When someone reports preferring one alternative over another, a natural expectation is that the model raises the preferred alternative’s valuation and lowers the other’s. The paper calls this property monotonicity. Many commonly used comparison-based preference models lack that guarantee, even though their purpose is to learn from precisely these comparisons.

Previously established monotone algorithms belonged to the Generalized Bradley-Terry family, which could not generalize to alternatives absent from comparisons. The authors introduce Linear Generalized Bradley-Terry models with Diffusion Priors to investigate how generalization and monotonicity can coexist. Their theoretical contribution identifies sufficient conditions on the alternatives’ embeddings that guarantee monotonicity.

The conditions matter: the paper does not claim that all embeddings or all generalizing preference models have this property. Experiments indicate that monotonicity is far from automatic, while the proposed model class improves prediction accuracy, especially with limited data. The contribution combines a conditional behavioral guarantee with an approach that can transfer information to uncompared alternatives, linking how a model reacts to feedback with how broadly it can use that feedback.
neurips-2025-generalizing-while-preservi.tldr: The paper gives sufficient embedding conditions for preference models that generalize to uncompared alternatives while preserving monotone responses to comparisons.

paragraphs: Graph anomaly detection often builds a detector for each individual graph. IA-GGAD instead targets a generalist detector that can identify anomalies on previously unseen graphs. The paper separates the transfer challenge into changes in node features and changes in graph structure, and introduces quantitative measures of how severe these shifts are.

Two learning modules address those sources of mismatch. An anomaly-driven invariant module learns node representations intended to remain useful across domains despite differing feature spaces. A structure-insensitive affinity module captures cross-domain structural correspondences using affinity-based features. Combining them allows the framework to predict anomalies without retraining or fine-tuning on the target graph.

Experiments across benchmark datasets from varied domains report better performance than state-of-the-art methods, including an AUROC improvement of up to 12.28% over ARC on ACM. Ablation studies support the contribution of each module. The results suggest that treating feature and structural shifts separately can help a single detector transfer across graphs, with the reported gains established on the evaluated datasets.
neurips-2025-ia-ggad-zero-shot-generalis.tldr: IA-GGAD combines invariant node representations and affinity-based structural features to detect anomalies on unseen graphs without target-domain tuning.

paragraphs: Generative behavior cloning learns robot behavior through models that generate actions. Diffusion policies often produce several actions at once and execute that sequence without replanning. This open-loop approach can perform well, but random action generation sometimes produces errors, and committing to a sequence delays responses to changes in the environment.

The paper introduces two complementary improvements. Self-guidance uses past observations to improve the fidelity of generated actions while implicitly encouraging behavior that accounts for the future. Adaptive chunking decides when to update an action sequence, weighing the benefit of reacting to new information against the value of keeping actions consistent over time.

Together, these techniques address both what the policy generates and how long the robot follows that generation before revising it. Experiments across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks report substantial improvements in generative behavior cloning. The findings support managing consistency and reactivity jointly: a robot benefits from reliable sequences while retaining the ability to change course when feedback makes an update worthwhile.
neurips-2025-improving-generative-behavi.tldr: Self-guidance and adaptive action chunking improve diffusion-policy reliability and responsiveness across simulated and real robotic manipulation tasks.

paragraphs: Giving a model more inference-time work can mean generating longer reasoning sequences or sampling multiple answers. Kinetics argues that evaluating these strategies through computation alone overestimates smaller models’ efficiency because memory access also matters. The authors analyze models ranging from 0.6 billion to 32 billion parameters using both kinds of cost.

Their proposed scaling law suggests that additional inference-time compute is more effective for models above a 14-billion-parameter threshold than for smaller models. In this analysis, attention becomes the dominant cost factor. That motivates sparse attention, which lowers the cost per generated token and allows longer generations or more parallel samples under the same resource budget.

Experiments on AIME and LiveCodeBench report that sparse-attention models outperform dense counterparts, with gains exceeding 60 points in low-cost regimes and five points in high-cost regimes. The findings favor allocating resources according to computation and memory together. The threshold and advantages arise from the reported analysis and experiments, while the authors’ broader conclusion is that sparse attention is central to realizing test-time scaling’s potential.
neurips-2025-kinetics-rethinking-test-ti.tldr: Kinetics incorporates memory-access costs into test-time scaling and finds substantial efficiency and accuracy benefits from sparse attention.

paragraphs: MIR-Bench evaluates whether language models can infer complicated patterns from many examples placed in their context. The motivation is a gap between short pattern-recognition tests and long-context evaluations: the former usually provide few examples, while many of the latter emphasize classification or finding information rather than integrating evidence into a rule.

The benchmark presents input-output examples generated by underlying functions in diverse data formats, then asks models to predict outputs for new inputs. This setup examines learning within the prompt, without fine-tuning. It makes the relationship among examples central to solving the task, providing a setting for studying reasoning over hundreds or thousands of demonstrations.

The authors use MIR-Bench to investigate scaling, robustness, retrieval augmentation, coding-based induction, and generalization across domains. They also examine inductive reasoning, which seeks a general rule, versus transductive reasoning directed at the requested prediction. The abstract identifies these research directions without stating their individual outcomes. The contribution is an evaluation framework for testing how extended context supports pattern learning and application.
neurips-2025-mir-bench-can-your-llm-reco.tldr: MIR-Bench tests whether language models can integrate many input-output examples to infer and apply complicated patterns.

paragraphs: This paper studies how Transformers learn from examples in a prompt when those examples describe Markovian dynamics. Such structured problems extend beyond the independent inputs and linear regression tasks emphasized by earlier theory. The authors analyze the optimization landscape of linear self-attention models to understand both their optimal solutions and the difficulty of realizing them.

For a single attention layer, they derive a closed-form global minimizer in an enlarged parameter space. However, recovering Transformer parameters that implement that solution is NP-hard in general. The distinction is consequential: expressing an optimum in a broader mathematical space does not make obtaining corresponding model parameters computationally straightforward.

The paper also interprets multilayer linear self-attention as carrying out preconditioned gradient descent across multiple objectives, extending beyond squared error. Numerical experiments with simplified Transformers validate the theoretical results. These findings give a more detailed account of in-context learning for dynamical functions, while keeping the hardness claim tied to the analyzed one-layer setting rather than asserting that every Transformer learning problem is intractable.
neurips-2025-optimality-and-np-hardness-.tldr: The paper characterizes optimal linear-attention learning of Markovian functions and proves that recovering parameters for the one-layer optimum is NP-hard in general.

paragraphs: Physics-informed neural networks incorporate physical equations into learning, but their accuracy and scalability can deteriorate in difficult geometries. This paper targets intersecting three-dimensional fluid channels with high aspect ratios. The resulting flows include deflection, mixing, and recirculation, creating a demanding setting for a learned surrogate.

The proposed approach divides the channel volume into roughly cubic subdomains, each handled by its own network. This reduces the complexity assigned to each model. A further global constraint requires total incoming mass flow to equal total outgoing mass flow. The resulting MDPINN-GD framework combines local modeling with a physical consistency requirement spanning the entire domain.

The authors report accuracy improvements of 74.8% over a single-network PINN and 52.9% over a multi-domain version without global mass conservation. Velocity predictions compared with simulations have maximum normalized mean absolute errors below 14.9%, including complex intersection and outlet regions. These results support combining decomposition with global constraints; extension to broader multiphysics and high-dimensional problems is presented as a future direction.
neurips-2025-physics-informed-machine-le.tldr: Dividing complex fluid channels among multiple PINNs and enforcing global mass conservation improves the reported accuracy of 3D flow predictions.

paragraphs: PDFuse combines information from multiple source images using a pretrained latent diffusion model without additional training. It treats fusion as a generation process constrained by those sources. The challenge is to retain their information while also benefiting from the model’s learned ability to generate high-quality images.

Two mechanisms regulate that process. Multi-source Information Consistency Projection links the model’s latent representations to source images and uses conjugate gradients to efficiently inject source information. Latent Manifold-preservation Guidance aligns latent distributions with those of the sources while respecting the diffusion model’s learned prior. Alternating the mechanisms coordinates source fidelity and generative quality.

The framework also incorporates a set of interference operators into both mechanisms to address degraded inputs during fusion. This does not require clean images to supervise new training. Experiments report highly competitive performance across varied fusion tasks and image modalities. The work shows how constraining inference can adapt an existing generative model to fusion while jointly addressing source consistency and image degradation.
neurips-2025-projection-manifold-regular.tldr: PDFuse uses alternating source-consistency and latent-distribution constraints to perform image fusion with a pretrained diffusion model and no additional training.

paragraphs: State-space models such as Mamba offer efficient sequence processing, but increasing their expressive capacity through mixtures of experts is not straightforward. The paper reports that naive combinations can fail or degrade performance. Routing Mamba addresses this by concentrating sparse expert capacity in linear projection layers.

The architecture uses mixtures of linear projection experts while sharing routing decisions between projection layers and sharing lightweight Mamba submodules across experts. This design coordinates expert use within the layer. It expands the total parameter pool while activating only part of that pool, aiming to improve language modeling without paying the computation cost of a comparably large dense model.

With 1.3 billion active parameters out of 10 billion total and a training sequence length of 16,000, RoM matches a dense Mamba model needing over 2.3 times as many active parameters. It also shows consistent perplexity across context lengths. Experiments on hybrid language models report 23% fewer floating-point operations than dense Mamba scaling at similar performance, supporting the efficiency of this particular expert-sharing design.
neurips-2025-routing-mamba-scaling-state.tldr: Routing Mamba scales capacity through sparse projection experts, matching larger dense models with fewer active parameters and lower reported computation.

paragraphs: Biological sequence models need explanations that reveal which sequence features influence predictions and how features interact. Shapley-based explanations provide a principled approach, but repeatedly computing them across thousands of sequences is expensive. SHAP zero targets this repeated-query cost so that local explanations can support broader investigations of model behavior.

The method performs a one-time sketching step that summarizes the model for subsequent explanations. It exploits a connection among Shapley values, interactions involving multiple features, and the model’s sparse Fourier transform. By paying an upfront cost and reusing the resulting sketch, it makes future queries nearly free at the margin rather than recomputing each explanation independently.

Applications cover models of guide RNA efficacy, DNA repair outcomes, and protein fitness. The authors report explanation speeds orders of magnitude faster than existing methods and recovery of combinatorial interactions that were previously inaccessible at scale. The near-zero claim concerns additional queries after sketching. The contribution is a reusable explanation computation that makes large-scale analysis of black-box sequence models more practical.
neurips-2025-shap-zero-explains-biologic.tldr: SHAP zero amortizes biological sequence explanations through a one-time model sketch, enabling near-zero marginal cost for later queries.

paragraphs: Monte Carlo Tree Search can produce reasoning examples for training language models, but conventional pipelines often retain only the highest-scoring path. SIGMA examines the information lost when neighboring branches are discarded. Those branches can contain useful partial reasoning, alternative strategies, or repeated mistakes even when they do not provide the best complete answer.

The framework links sibling nodes along a search path and refines the selected trajectory in two stages. A critique model compares the siblings to identify strengths and weaknesses. A revision model then uses that feedback to improve the top-scoring trajectory through text-based backpropagation. The process turns otherwise discarded search material into guidance for a better training example.

On MATH, a SIGMA-tuned seven-billion-parameter model achieves 54.92% accuracy using 30,000 samples, outperforming the reported state-of-the-art comparisons trained on 590,000 samples. This result supports the value of extracting more supervision from existing search trees. Its central finding is that careful comparative refinement can improve reasoning while substantially reducing the amount of training data used in the reported comparison.
neurips-2025-sigma-refining-large-langua.tldr: SIGMA improves reasoning training data by using discarded sibling search branches to critique and revise the highest-scoring trajectory.

paragraphs: STEER-ME evaluates microeconomic reasoning beyond individual applications such as stock picking or financial analysis. It focuses on non-strategic settings, complementing earlier work on strategic decision-making. The authors organize the subject into 58 reasoning elements, with each grounded in combinations drawn from up to ten domains, five perspectives, and three types.

To populate this large space, auto-STEER uses language models to adapt handwritten question templates to new domains and perspectives. Generating fresh questions increases diversity and could reduce contamination from previously encountered benchmark material. That is a potential benefit of the generation process, rather than a guarantee that contamination is eliminated.

The benchmark evaluates 27 language models across scales and adaptation strategies, using multiple-choice and free-text questions with different scoring schemes. Results reveal systematic weaknesses in transferring economic reasoning across types, answer formats, and textual changes. The work provides a structured way to assess whether economic competence persists across variations in presentation and context, helping distinguish broad reasoning ability from success on a particular task format.
neurips-2025-steer-me-assessing-the-micr.tldr: STEER-ME evaluates 58 elements of microeconomic reasoning and finds systematic generalization weaknesses across 27 language models.

paragraphs: TP-MDDN introduces a navigation benchmark in which an embodied agent must satisfy multiple needs while respecting explicit task preferences. This extends single-demand navigation to longer activities involving several sub-demands. The challenge includes deciding what to pursue, maintaining progress across goals, and navigating an environment while responding to failures.

The proposed AWMSystem divides these responsibilities among three modules. BreakLLM decomposes instructions, LocateLLM selects goals, and StatusMLLM monitors task progress. Spatial memory comes from MASMap, which combines accumulated three-dimensional point clouds with two-dimensional semantic maps. This gives the system a representation of both spatial structure and meaningful environmental content.

Action generation combines zero-shot planning with policy-based fine control through a Dual-Tempo framework. An Adaptive Error Corrector handles failures as they occur. Experiments report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in perception accuracy and navigation robustness. The paper contributes both a task setting that makes multiple demands and preferences explicit and an integrated system for coordinating interpretation, mapping, planning, control, and monitoring over extended navigation.
neurips-2025-tp-mddn-task-preferenced-mu.tldr: TP-MDDN benchmarks navigation with multiple preferred demands, and AWMSystem combines task decomposition, spatial memory, planning, and error correction to address it.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks can lose accuracy when node attributes are noisy. The paper argues that common robustness methods make an overly restrictive assumption: feature noise is independent of graph structure and node labels. In the proposed dependency-aware noise setting, corruption participates in a chain of dependencies extending to both structure and labels.

The authors formalize this setting as DANG and develop DA-GNN to model it. The model uses variational inference to capture causal relationships among variables in the assumed data-generating process. This gives the learning method a way to account for linked sources of corruption, rather than treating noisy attributes as isolated from the rest of the graph.

The paper also introduces benchmark datasets that simulate these dependencies in real-world application settings. Experiments report that DA-GNN consistently outperforms existing baselines under both DANG and conventional noise models. The results support studying robustness through the relationships among corrupted quantities, with the benchmark contribution making this broader noise setting available for further evaluation.
neurips-2025-training-robust-graph-neura.tldr: DA-GNN models dependencies connecting feature noise, graph structure, and labels, improving reported robustness across dependent and conventional noise settings.

paragraphs: TreeGen models distributions over hierarchies, allowing it to generate alternative tree structures rather than produce only one fixed organization. The paper extends Bayesian Flow Networks to this setting. Its representation uses categorical distributions to connect uncertain, probabilistic hierarchies with concrete discrete trees.

A key component is a scheduler that controls how uncertainty decreases during generation. The proposed schedule produces smooth, consistent entropy reduction even when the number of categories varies. This matters within the framework because different categorical choices need a coordinated progression from uncertainty toward a specific hierarchy. The scheduler supports that progression across differently sized choice sets.

The empirical evaluation concerns jet clustering in high-energy physics. TreeGen consistently produces valid trees satisfying physical constraints, with log-likelihoods close to those of the ground truth. The authors also compare generated samples with the exact posterior distribution and use rejection sampling for likelihood maximization, reporting better performance than several baselines. These findings support the framework’s ability to represent and generate physically meaningful hierarchies in the evaluated task.
neurips-2025-treegen-a-bayesian-generati.tldr: TreeGen extends Bayesian Flow Networks to hierarchical generation and produces valid, physically constrained trees in jet-clustering experiments.

paragraphs: UFO brings detailed visual perception into a shared language-based interface. Object detection, pixel-level segmentation, and image-level vision-language tasks often require separate architectural machinery. The paper aims to simplify this arrangement by translating their prediction targets into the language space, allowing a single model to address all three levels.

Segmentation is supported by an embedding retrieval method that operates solely through that language interface. This is the mechanism that helps the unified design reach pixel-level outputs. The framework also integrates with existing multimodal language models, connecting detailed perception with their language abilities for tasks such as reasoning segmentation.

After joint training on five visual perception datasets, UFO exceeds previous generalist models by 12.3 mAP on COCO instance segmentation and 3.3 mIoU on ADE20K semantic segmentation. The authors also report comparable or better performance than methods with elaborate task-specific designs and stronger reasoning-segmentation performance after integration with multimodal models. These results support language as a practical common interface for visual tasks that operate at very different levels of detail.
neurips-2025-ufo-a-unified-approach-to-f.tldr: UFO unifies detection, segmentation, and vision-language tasks through a language interface while improving reported generalist-model segmentation performance.

paragraphs: The paper investigates why asking models to reason step by step can hurt video understanding. Its analysis finds that chain-of-thought often produces long but misleading explanations, introduces visual details absent from the video, and overrides initially correct judgments. The authors call this pattern visual thinking drift.

They propose a Bayesian interpretation: reasoning can move away from observed visual evidence and amplify internal biases or language-based expectations. Under this account, an increasingly elaborate explanation may reflect a plausible story rather than what happened on screen. This is presented as an explanation of the observed drift, not a claim that every reasoning trace has this problem.

To counter it, Visual Evidence Reward uses reinforcement learning to reward reasoning traces that can be verified against visual evidence. The resulting Video-VER model consistently achieves top performance across ten video-understanding benchmarks in the reported evaluation. The findings support training the evidential quality of intermediate reasoning, so that additional reasoning remains connected to the video instead of merely becoming more fluent or detailed.
neurips-2025-when-thinking-drifts-eviden.tldr: Video-VER rewards visually grounded reasoning to counter the misleading chain-of-thought drift observed in video-understanding models.

paragraphs: X2-DFD aims to help multimodal language models detect deepfakes and explain their decisions. It starts by assessing which forgery-related features a model can detect, producing a prioritized ranking based on their importance to that model. This assessment guides subsequent training around the model’s demonstrated strengths and gaps.

The next stage builds an explainable dataset through two complementary processes. Strong Feature Strengthening reinforces features the model already understands well. Weak Feature Supplementing incorporates specialized detectors, such as low-level artifact analyzers, to supply information the language model handles poorly. The model is then fine-tuned on the constructed dataset and used for both detection and explanation.

Experiments, ablations, and a human study report improvements over the original multimodal models. The architecture is also designed to accept future models and specialized detectors as replaceable components. This makes extension an explicit design goal: as detection tools develop, the framework is intended to incorporate them while preserving its process of assessing capabilities, supplementing weaknesses, and training for explainable decisions.
neurips-2025-x2-dfd-a-framework-for-expl.tldr: X2-DFD improves deepfake detection and explanations by reinforcing a multimodal model’s strong features and supplementing weak ones with specialized detectors.
